mission: Make the Mac/iPhone benchmark truly one command: audit tools/mac-bench for bit-rot at integration head, compile/schema-check and dry-run everything that does not need Apple hardware, profile the Linux-measurable pipeline pieces at head with counts, and commit an updated harness + runbook so hardware availability means immediate execution. Apple-execution-dependent paths stay BLOCKED_EXTERNAL.
method: bash -n syntax audit of run-mac-bench.sh and exercised the Linux refusal path (expected exit 3)
package typecheck (tsc --noEmit) and full unit suite for @pickle/mac-bench at head
dry-ran every non-Apple path: compare CLI on fixture documents, assembleResults with synthetic samples, schema validation of mac-bench-results-v1
diffed the harness stage-harvest map against the CURRENT analyzeVideo timing vocabulary to find drift

wrote tools/mac-bench/src/profileLinuxPieces.ts and measured decode, frame extraction, file I/O, JSON parse/stringify, and real two-pass schedule planning (planTwoPassSchedule, paddle-two-pass-1) on Linux at head
committed RUNBOOK.md describing the exact one-command Mac procedure and the Linux-verified vs Mac-only boundary

datasetScope.grouping: committed dev event-window bundle clips only; profiling is per-clip, no cross-clip aggregation
datasetScope.twoPassScheduleInput: SYNTHETIC sparse tracks derived only from real clip metadata (fps, durationMs); measures scheduling mechanics, not detector accuracy — labeled synthetic in the artifact

holdoutStatement: The held-out cases are excluded by name from all profiling inputs (the profiler hard-fails if a held-out ID appears in its clip list). Nothing in this workstream read, listed, executed, or tuned against held-out material.

linuxProfileHighlights.boundary: LINUX-CPU-NOT-MAC — never a substitute for Mac results
linuxProfileHighlights.jsonSerialization: all three committed artifacts (1.8–3.6 KB) parse+stringify in <0.02 ms mean over 20 iterations — negligible against decode

twoPassScheduleMechanics.inputProvenance: SYNTHETIC sparse track derived from real clip metadata

findings: BIT-ROT FOUND AND FIXED: the harness stage-harvest map (runCase.ts REPORT_TIMING_STAGES) lagged the current analyzeVideo timing vocabulary — poseDerivativesMs and the two-pass split timings (paddleDetectSparseMs, paddleDetectDenseMs) were emitted by the pipeline but silently dropped by the bench. A Mac run at head would have lost those stages. Now harvested, with regression tests.

BIT-ROT FOUND AND FIXED: a lab:cascade output with 0 gold events (canonical runs / gold absent) crashed result assembly at the very end of a bench run (schema requires goldEvents >= 1). Assembly now converts zero-gold cascade to cascade: null with an explicit cascadeUnmeasuredReason, preserving the latency evidence — missing evidence stays absent, never zero.
Everything else audited clean at head: shell syntax, Linux refusal (exit 3), 38/38 package tests, package tsc clean, compare CLI VERDICT: OK on fixtures, mac-bench-results-v1 schema validation.

Linux-measurable costs at head are small relative to the Mac-only stages: full-clip decode ~0.2 s and JPEG frame extraction ~0.5–0.7 s per dev clip, JSON serialization negligible; two-pass scheduling itself costs ~0.03 ms and plans 78/132 and 96/201 frames (2 clips) with 4 detector process invocations vs 1 single-pass — the frame-count saving is what the Mac run will actually feel.

Apple-execution-dependent items remain BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: Swift extractor build, Apple Vision pose extraction, real cold/warm Mac latency, lab:regen/lab:cascade with gold evidence, and all iPhone device numbers. No such numbers are reported anywhere in this workstream.
rationale: Everything Linux-checkable is verified at head with counts (38/38 package tests, refusal path, compare dry-run, schema validation, measured Linux profile with explicit N), and two real bit-rot defects that would have degraded or crashed a Mac run were fixed with tests. GREEN cannot be claimed because the one command itself has still never executed on Apple hardware — that execution, and every number it would produce, is BLOCKED_EXTERNAL.
